summary.text: Maggie Goodlander is the Democratic incumbent in New Hampshire's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in November 2024. A Nashua native, she worked as a Senate foreign policy advisor, Navy Reserve intelligence officer, Supreme Court law clerk, constitutional law instructor, Justice Department deputy assistant attorney general and White House senior advisor before running for Congress. She sits on the House Armed Services and Small Business Committees.

paragraphs.text: Maggie Goodlander was born in Nashua, New Hampshire, in 1986, and her House biography says she was raised there, where her family has lived for more than 100 years.
She earned a bachelor's degree in history from Yale University in 2009 and a J.D. from Yale Law School in 2016.
She began her career as a senior foreign policy advisor to U.S. Senators Joe Lieberman and John McCain, and her House biography says she helped write sanctions legislation.
Goodlander served as an intelligence officer in the U.S. Navy Reserve for 11 years, according to her House biography.

After law school she clerked for Justice Stephen Breyer on the U.S. Supreme Court, then returned to New Hampshire to teach constitutional law at the University of New Hampshire and Dartmouth. Her House biography says she served as counsel in the first impeachment of President Donald Trump.

She later served as a deputy assistant attorney general at the U.S. Department of Justice, where her House biography says she worked on cases involving corporate monopolies, and as a senior advisor at the White House, where she led the Unity Agenda (opioids, mental health, Big Tech, veterans, and cancer).

Goodlander won the September 10, 2024 Democratic primary for the open 2nd District seat over Colin Van Ostern, then defeated Republican Lily Williams 52.9% to 47.0% in the November 2024 general election.
In the 119th Congress (2025-2026) she is assigned to the House Armed Services Committee (Military Personnel; Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittees) and the Small Business Committee.
She has served as a board member of the NH Women's Foundation, NH Legal Assistance, and the World Affairs Council of New Hampshire, and on the Rudman Center Advisory Board.
